messages:
julie: FYI a DSAR landed for user 0x4f7c asking full deletion of account data. Trouble: we have an active vuln triage that flagged possible identifier leakage in embeddings and we recently shipped a snapshot to s3 encrypted with customer-keystore. Legal is asking for a temporary forensics hold. Need clear steps for retention exception + KMS handling.

nate: ok. first question — can Legal approve a timeboxed hold? we should avoid an open-ended exception. also need to know which assets: embeddings index, S3 snapshots, audit logs, and any in-flight caches?

julie: Legal says they can approve up to 90 days for forensic analysis, must be logged and auditable. Affected assets: embeddings index (rdw-emb-2026-03), s3://prod-user-snapshots/2026-03-14, and recent request logs in elk.

sara: Proposal: create a retention-exception ticket with an explicit expiry timestamp, add an immutable audit entry, and limit delete permissions via RBAC (only privacy@ can execute deletion after hold expires). Also mark the user in our DSAR tracker as 'hold'.

leo: For KMS: current snapshots are encrypted with key alias/rdw/prod/snap-2023 which is on automatic rotation. If we rotate the key now, older backups might still be decryptable but we risk complicating key recovery. I'd prefer we export a copy of the snapshot wrapped with a stable forensic KMS key (alias/rdw/forensics) and lock its key policy so only sec-eng+legal role can read.

julie: +1 to export. Can infra run export and lock key policy? Also how do we ensure embedding records in the vector DB are frozen for investigation without accidental purge?

leo: Steps I recommend:
1) Create a read-only forensic bucket s3://forensics-hold/1864507890 and copy the affected snapshots there using aws kms:Encrypt with alias/rdw/forensics.
2) Snapshot the embeddings index and export to newline-delimited JSON with user_id hashed, but keep the raw copy in the forensic bucket.
3) Update object ACLs and bucket policy to only allow sec-eng and legal roles. Enable S3 Object Lock with Governance mode for 90 days.
4) Do NOT rotate the forensic key during the hold window.

legal-team: We'll draft the hold authorization email and attach the signed exception. Legal requires the hold record to include: requester, reason, assets, expiry, and approver. Also want an audit trail of who accessed the forensic bucket.

julie: RBAC change needed: create temporary role 'forensics-read' with minimal privileges to read s3://forensics-hold/* and read-only access to embeddings snapshots. Add MFA enforcement. After copy, restrict existing delete action for embeddings to a deny for anyone except privacy-admin which will be allowed only when hold expires.

sara: Can we add an automated audit event when that RBAC role is created/assigned? we should log role grants to the audit pipeline. Proposed audit event format: `event_type: retention_exception_grant, actor, target_assets, ttl_seconds, ticket_id`.

audit-bot: retention-exception-created id=REX-2026-1864507890 by=julie expiry=1866796890 assets=[rdw-emb-2026-03,s3://prod-user-snapshots/2026-03-14,elk-req-logs] severity=high

nate: quick operational Q: how do we reconcile this with the DSAR regulatory requirement to delete data asap? We need to show Legal the conflict and rationale for the temporary exception. Also update the DSAR tracker note.

legal-team: DSAR timeline acknowledged. We'll log the exception and notify the requester with a delay notice citing ongoing investigation. Keep the delay minimal and timeboxed.

julie: vuln triage note: the suspected leakage is an embedding similarity leak that may include user identifiers in prompts. We should run a prompt/minimization eval across recent batches to scope affected user_ids. If we can scope and delete only affected vectors we might shorten the hold.

leo: I'll run an eval job and produce a list of vector IDs that map to user_ids. Output will go to the forensic bucket and to the secure ticket. Expect results in ~2h.

sara: after we have vector IDs we should run a targeted deletion API call. Example (dev-only):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/internal/embeddings/delete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vector_ids": ["v123","v456"], "reason": "dsar-targeted-removal"}'
```
Make sure the call writes an audit event and we snapshot the pre-deletion index.

julie: To summarize action items: leo export snapshots -> forensic bucket (immediate), sara create RBAC deny rules + audit hooks, legal sign hold + update DSAR tracker, leo run eval job (2h), sara prepare targeted deletion flow and confirm audit events, julie to open retention-exception ticket and notify requester.

nate: I will update DSAR tracker and draft the requester notification. tagged @legal-team for sign-off once evidence scope is available.

legal-team: acknowledged. Please ensure all actions and timestamps are recorded in the exception record. We'll revisit before expiry to either release the hold or extend with justification.

julie: thanks everyone. I'll post the retention-exception ticket link in this thread when created and ping again when exports complete. :thumbsup:
